references.text: The city of refuge was to protect the manslayer from the avenger of blood until he could stand trial before the assembly.
The six cities of refuge were designated as places where someone who had killed another unintentionally could seek asylum.
Joshua reiterates the rule that the manslayer must remain in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest.
The basic law concerning cities of refuge for unintentional killing was first given in the covenant at Sinai.
Anointing the high priest with holy oil was a consecration act that made him the highest religious leader.
The high priest was anointed with the holy oil and held a special position among the priests.
Deuteronomy expands on the laws regarding cities of refuge and the protection of one who kills unintentionally.
Joshua carries out the provisions concerning the cities of refuge that were given through Moses.
The book of Hebrews uses the image of refuge as a symbol of the salvation and security believers have in Christ.
